title: Cut six complete cookies from one sheet of rolled dough without overlapping the cuts
instruction: Cut six complete cookies from the rolled dough with the round cutter. Keep each cut inside the dough and separate from the others. Set the cutter down beside the dough.
context: Cut-out cookies are stamped straight down from an already-rolled dough slab. The baker must leave enough material around every cut and fit the cutter without crossing an earlier outline. Running the rim through the entire thickness frees the shape. A partial impression or overlap leaves shapes that cannot be lifted out whole.
setup: Station table, positions in cm from the midpoint between arm bases, with x forward and y toward the left arm. Center a flat 20.7 × 16.4 × 0.6 cm wood pastry board at (33.4, −0.1). Center a fresh 19.8 × 13.7 cm sheet of recipe-defined short dough, 4.2 mm thick at 4 ± 1 °C, on the board. Put a 5.2 cm round, 3 cm high stainless cutter with its rolled lip up at (30.6, −16.3). Arms ready, grippers open.
scoring: 0.125 per complete through-cut circle, through the entire circumference to the board, up to 0.75. Each circle needs at least 1 mm clearance from the slab edge and prior circles. An overlapping through-cut or one across the edge invalidates the trial. 1.0 when six valid cuts and the cutter rests at least 7 mm from the slab on the bench with both hands clear for at least 1 s. Judge spacing from above with a scale in frame. After the trial lift each disc with a thin turner to verify that no section remains attached.
reset_notes: Use the published short-dough formula in README.md. Roll between 4.2 mm guides, trim to 19.8 × 13.7 cm, and chill flat for 30 min. Verify 4 ± 1 °C on a same-thickness scrap at the start. Use a fresh sheet and clean, dry cutter each trial. For shared robot hardware, use removable washable silicone fingertip covers.
fidelity: The 4.2 mm slab applies a depth-dependent load and torque around the cutter rim. A published force–depth curve measured on the same dough with a straight wire scales to the engaged length of the ring. Every rim sector must reach the board during the same stamp with cutter–board contact, allowing 0.22 mm of solver clearance. A visible seam records the completed through-cut on the rigid slab. The physical lift test verifies separation.
scores: Dream-1 scored 0.0 in 1,200 steps. The scripted demo reached 1.0 in 613 steps. The shallow-press control scored 0.0 in 650 steps and the overlapping-cut control scored 0.0 in 300 steps.
